slides.title: Pelican Packaging: reserve, build or bridge?

paragraphs.text: Pelican Packaging: reserve, build or bridge?
Recommendation on the second molding-line installation slot, the full line order and temporary overflow capacity
Investment Committee pre-read  |  for decision at the January 2027 IC
Prepared November 2026  |  Built only from the IC briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); no external research

slides.title: Reserve the slot as a capped $0.6M option, bridge 2028 with the contract molder, and order the line only once signed demand and funding clear set triggers

paragraphs.text: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Reserve the slot as a capped $0.6M option, bridge 2028 with the contract molder, and order the line only once signed demand and funding clear set triggers
The gap is real and starts in 2028, but its size hinges on unsigned demand
•  Measured on accepted units, the line is 92% utilized in 2027, not 83%; overflow starts in 2028 (0.6M units)
•  At forecast, overflow reaches 3.5M units by 2030. At signed minimums it is only 0.9M; 2.6M of 2030 volume is unsigned
•  The 98% fill rate is measured monthly; two misses let a customer rebid its whole allocation
Ordering now breaks the cash covenant; doing nothing breaks the fill-rate standard
•  A full order leaves $4.0M of cash against the $7.0M floor ($3.0M short), and no borrowing facility exists
•  Doing nothing leaves 0.6M units unserved at the 2028 peak and 3.5M by 2030
•  The molder covers 2028-29 for $0.07-0.27M a year, but at forecast it falls 1.0M units short in 2030 and cannot make the specialty product
The slot is a capped option worth buying, provided the order date can move
•  Cash stays $1.2M above the floor; the most we can lose is the $0.6M deposit
•  It pays for itself only by protecting customer allocations. On incremental margin alone it does not
•  As offered, the slot expects an order by June 2027, but funding is only plausible in 2028. Agree a later order date before paying
Three hard triggers turn the reservation into a full order
•  Demand: signed 2029 or 2030 minimums of 10.5M units or more (today 9.4M / 9.8M), or a simulated fill-rate breach in 2+ months
•  Funding: at least $3.5M committed, so cash after the $4.2M payment stays at $7.5M or more
•  Readiness: supplier dates and the specialty validation plan confirmed. Target decision Q1 2028, last possible date Q3 2028
Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. Cash figures exclude 2027-30 operating cash flow, which the pack does not give.

slides.title: The starting hypothesis (reserve now, gate the order) survives the tests, but only with a funding plan and a flexible order date

paragraphs.text: HOW WE TESTED THE ANSWER
The starting hypothesis (reserve now, gate the order) survives the tests, but only with a funding plan and a flexible order date

data: What would have to be true
H1  A full order now does not fit within the covenant
H2  2028 overflow can be served without the new line
0.6M units of overflow vs the molder's 2.5M ceiling; 5 months' notice needed; specialty volume not yet in 2028
H3  Demand beyond the molder's reach is credible within the line's lead time
At forecast, 2030 overflow is 3.5M (1.0M over the ceiling). At signed minimums it is 0.9M. Two programs slipped a quarter last year
H4  The slot is affordable and its downside is capped
$8.8M - $0.6M = $8.2M, still $1.2M above the floor; the most we can lose is the forfeited $0.6M
H5  The $4.2M balance can be funded when the order must be placed
No committed facility. The prepayment / signed-volume loan is uncontracted and the CFO sees it in 2028
H6  The slot secures timing we could not get without it
The slot reserves an installation crew, not capacity. The pack gives no lead time without a slot; its timeline assumes an order by June 2027

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. Starting hypothesis = Operations Director's proposal: reserve the slot, release the machine only after signed orders and a liquidity review.

slides.title: Measured on accepted units, the line is already 92% utilized in 2027 and overflows from 2028; the '17% free capacity' view divides by nameplate output

paragraphs.text: 1  THE NEED
Measured on accepted units, the line is already 92% utilized in 2027 and overflows from 2028; the '17% free capacity' view divides by nameplate output
Forecast good units vs capacity, millions
Nameplate 10.0M
Practical 9.0M
Why the Ops KPI misleads
•  It divides units started by nameplate hours and reports quality rejects separately, so it overstates headroom
•  Real 2027 slack is 0.7M units (7.8%), not 1.7M (17%)
•  Specialty runs scrap 4 points more than the standard mix, and the forecast has no allowance for it: about 0.09-0.10M units of capacity lost a year from 2029
Calculation: 20% x 11.2M = 2.24M specialty units x 4% = 0.09M (2030: 2.48M x 4% = 0.10M)
The plant has no real buffer for 2028 peaks: whatever the decision, the bridge has to be in place before the 2028 peak.
Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. Practical accepted capacity of 9.0M units is net of maintenance, validated changeovers and quality holds; nameplate is 10.0M.

slides.title: The size of the gap depends on unsigned demand: at forecast, overflow reaches 3.5M units by 2030; at signed minimums it is only 0.9M

paragraphs.text: 1  THE NEED
The size of the gap depends on unsigned demand: at forecast, overflow reaches 3.5M units by 2030; at signed minimums it is only 0.9M
Overflow above internal capacity, millions of accepted units
What drives the range
•  Unsigned volume: of the 12.4M units forecast for 2030, 2.6M (21%) sit above signed minimums and are nonbinding
•  Timing: two key design programs slipped a quarter last year; a one-year slip pushes the molder ceiling breach from 2030 to 2031
•  Mix: specialty volume adds roughly 0.1M units of overflow a year through extra scrap
Implication
Only the forecast case needs a second line before 2031. Committing $4.8M before customers sign is a bet on the top bar.
Forecast
Forecast slips one year
Signed minimums only
Molder ceiling 2.5M
The new line is needed only if unsigned demand arrives on time, so signed volume should trigger the order.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. Overflow = demand above 9.0M practical capacity plus the specialty scrap allowance (20% of 2029-30 units x 4%). Slip case = forecast delayed one year (assumption).

slides.title: Annual totals understate the risk: the 98% standard is measured monthly, and with the molder maxed out, 2029 runs at 98% of monthly supply

paragraphs.text: 1  THE NEED
Annual totals understate the risk: the 98% standard is measured monthly, and with the molder maxed out, 2029 runs at 98% of monthly supply
What the standard requires
Why annual capacity is not enough
What is at stake
•  A 98% fill rate every month, for every medical-device customer
•  Missing it twice gives the customer the right to rebid its whole supplier allocation, not just the units missed
•  Internal practical rate is ~0.75M units a month; the molder adds at most ~0.21M a month
•  Several customer launches inside one six-week window can exceed the monthly rate even when the year fits (plant supervisor)
•  The molder has not committed holiday-period capacity
•  Base business of 9.0M units x $0.45 = ~$4.0M of annual contribution exposed to a rebid (proxy)
•  Losing a quarter of it costs ~$1.0M a year, more than the $0.45M lost on the 2030 forecast shortfall itself
•  A monthly simulation or an inventory buffer is needed to confirm compliance

data: Demand as % of max monthly supply
How far a peak month can exceed the average

paragraphs.text: In 2029 even the molder bridge leaves only ~2% monthly headroom: a launch cluster could trigger the two misses that open a rebid.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. Monthly rates = annual capacity / 12 (even-flow simplification). Contribution proxy uses the pack's $0.45/unit for serving rather than refusing demand.

slides.title: Ordering the full line now would leave $4.0M of cash, $3.0M below the covenant floor, and the growth evidence offered for it does not show cause and effect

paragraphs.text: 2  THE OPTIONS
Ordering the full line now would leave $4.0M of cash, $3.0M below the covenant floor, and the growth evidence offered for it does not show cause and effect
Cash after 2027 commitments, $M
Floor $7.0M
The Sales VP's '23% faster growth' claim
•  It compares companies at one point in time: the early builders also held more advance purchase commitments and sold into faster-growing therapeutic segments
•  It cannot show that building capacity caused the growth, and the board will not accept 'demand is growing' as a reason to breach the floor
Do nothing
Molder only
Reserve slot
Order line now
With no facility, ordering in 2027 needs at least $3.0M of new funding. 'Order now' is ruled out on cash.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. Cash after 2027 commitments = $11.0M unrestricted - $2.2M approved validation/R&D - path commitment. Operating cash flow excluded (not in pack).

slides.title: Only 'reserve the slot + molder bridge' passes every hard constraint while keeping 2030 capacity available

paragraphs.text: 2  THE OPTIONS
Only 'reserve the slot + molder bridge' passes every hard constraint while keeping 2030 capacity available

data: Covered if triggers met by Q3 2028
$5.8M if ordered Q1 2028; $0.6M + premium if not

paragraphs.text: How the recommended path's $5.8M builds up: $4.8M line (deposit credited, not double-counted) + $0.07M molder premium in 2028 + $0.14M for H1 2029 + $0.83M fixed cost for mid-2029 to 2030. That is $0.6M less than ordering now, because fixed costs start about 18 months later.
Molder only is cheapest to 2029 but cannot meet forecast 2030 demand. Do nothing fails in the first peak.
Choosing 'reserve + bridge' over 'order now' costs nothing in capacity; it removes the covenant breach and a $4.8M bet on unsigned demand.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. Costs are 2027-30 incremental cash at forecast demand: capex, $0.55M/yr fixed cost from commissioning, molder premium $0.12/unit, lost contribution $0.45/unit. They exclude operating cash flow and value after 2030.

slides.title: The contract molder is a cheap bridge through 2029, but at forecast it runs out in 2030 and it cannot make the specialty product

paragraphs.text: 2  THE OPTIONS
The contract molder is a cheap bridge through 2029, but at forecast it runs out in 2030 and it cannot make the specialty product
Forecast overflow (incl. specialty scrap), millions of units
Ceiling 2.5M
Limits beyond the ceiling
•  Specialty (20% of 2029 units, 2.24M) is not validated at the molder, so it must run in-house and takes the internal slack
•  Five months' notice; holiday-period capacity not yet committed
•  Still worth using: serving through the molder keeps $0.33 of the $0.45 unit contribution, against $0 for a refused order
24% of ceiling
92% of ceiling
140%: 1.0M short
Use the molder to bridge 2028-29. It is not a substitute for the line if forecast 2030 demand arrives.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. Premium of $0.12/accepted unit excludes first-article validation for the specialty product. 2029 at 92% of the ceiling leaves 0.2M units of annual slack.

slides.title: The new line is insurance for customer allocations, not a margin play: it beats the molder on running cost only above 4.6M overflow units a year

paragraphs.text: 2  THE OPTIONS
The new line is insurance for customer allocations, not a margin play: it beats the molder on running cost only above 4.6M overflow units a year
Break-even overflow volume
units a year = $0.55M line fixed cost / $0.12 molder premium per unit
Forecast overflow peaks at 3.5M (2030), so within the molder's 2.5M ceiling, buying is cheaper than running a second line, even before the $4.8M capex
The line saves $0.12 per unit inside the ceiling, but $0.45 per unit beyond it
So the line earns only ~$0.20M a year more than the molder in 2030. The $4.8M is justified by what it protects:
•  Fill-rate compliance in peak months, which protects ~$4.0M a year of base contribution from rebids
•  In-house capacity for the specialty product the molder cannot make
•  Growth after 2030: each 1M units above the molder ceiling adds $0.45M a year to the line's advantage
Because the case rests on protecting allocations, the order trigger should be signed customer volume, not forecast margin.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. No salvage value, useful life or discount rate is given, so the comparison is on annual running economics only. $0.45 and $0.12 are not compared as if they were alternative price quotes.

slides.title: The slot is a capped option: it risks at most $0.6M, keeps $1.2M above the cash floor and pays off only if it heads off an allocation rebid

paragraphs.text: 3  THE SLOT DECISION
The slot is a capped option: it risks at most $0.6M, keeps $1.2M above the cash floor and pays off only if it heads off an allocation rebid

data: Equals ~5.5 years of the 2030 molder premium ($0.11M)
Loss avoided if 2030 capacity is late by one year

paragraphs.text: Cash test with the deposit paid
•  $8.8M - $0.6M = $8.2M, still $1.2M above the floor. The deposit uses a third of the $1.8M headroom, leaving room for 2028-29 molder premiums ($0.35M)
•  The deposit does not fund the line: the $4.2M balance still needs at least $3.0M of new money
How to read it
•  On lost units alone, the deposit would not be worth paying
•  It is worth paying if there is roughly a 1-in-4 to 2-in-5 chance that the slot is what keeps a customer's allocation. Today's 2.6M of unsigned 2030 volume and the 2028 overflow make that plausible
•  That chance is only real if the slot buys timing we could not otherwise get (H6)
Recommendation: pay the deposit as insurance, on condition that its order date can be deferred. Without that, the insurance lapses before funding arrives.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. Break-even probability = $0.6M at risk / loss avoided for one year of late capacity. Rebid shares are illustrative, applied to the 9.0M-unit base x $0.45 proxy.

slides.title: Reserving the slot becomes a bad option under five conditions; the two most likely can be tested before the March deposit

paragraphs.text: 3  THE SLOT DECISION
Reserving the slot becomes a bad option under five conditions; the two most likely can be tested before the March deposit

data: Condition that destroys the slot's value
1  The order must be placed by June 2027, while funding is only plausible in 2028
We would have to forfeit $0.6M or breach the covenant
Negotiate an order date of Q1 2028 or later (install H1 2029); otherwise decline
2  The slot buys nothing scarce: a 12-month lead time is available without it
Paying $0.6M for timing we would get anyway
Get written lead time and crew availability without a slot
Overflow of 0.9M or less through 2030; molder covers it for $0.11M a year or less
Track signed volume quarterly; kill at the go/no-go gate
The line arrives a year early and carries $0.55M a year of fixed cost before it is needed
Use the deferral right; molder covers 2030 at 92% of its ceiling
The deposit uses $0.6M of $1.8M headroom; pre-build stock and validation compete for the rest
13-week cash forecast; cap pre-build working capital

paragraphs.text: If the supplier will not move the order date to Q1 2028 or later, decline the slot and plan on the molder plus a 2028 order at standard lead time, once that lead time is confirmed.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. The pack gives no slot expiry or deferral terms; the June 2027 order date comes from the stated 'if ordered by June 2027, machine expected mid-2028'.

slides.title: Cover 2028 in three layers: the contract molder booked by June 2027, a 2027 safety stock, and specialty kept in-house

paragraphs.text: 4  THE PLAN AND GATES
Cover 2028 in three layers: the contract molder booked by June 2027, a 2027 safety stock, and specialty kept in-house
A. External capacity: contract molder
B. Internal buffer: 2027 safety stock
C. Internal mix: protect what only we can make
•  Book 0.6M units for 2028 (24% of the ceiling), about $0.07M of premium
•  Formal notice is 5 months, but sign by 30 June 2027 to lock in holiday-period capacity
•  Hold an option on up to 2.3M units for 2029 (~$0.27M)
•  Get a quote and timeline for specialty first-article validation as a hedge
•  2027 has 0.7M units of practical slack (9.0M - 8.3M), more than the 2028 overflow
•  Pre-build standard containers ahead of the 2028 peak to absorb launch clustering
•  Depends on shelf-life and customer lot rules; cap the working capital so cash headroom holds
•  Schedule specialty first on the own line; the molder is not validated for it
•  Add a 4-point specialty scrap allowance to the plan (~0.1M units a year)
•  Run a monthly fill-rate simulation (launch windows, holidays, scrap) by Q2 2027

data: Working capital (unit cost not in pack)

paragraphs.text: Only a January 2027 order, which breaches the covenant, gets the line in before the 2028 peak; any compliant order arrives after it, so 2028 needs this bridge.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. The pack says the 2028 peak starts before mid-2028; we assume around Q2 2028, so the latest molder notice is about November 2027. Unit cost for pre-build not given.

slides.title: Release the $4.2M balance only when all three triggers are met: demand, funding and readiness

paragraphs.text: 4  THE PLAN AND GATES
Release the $4.2M balance only when all three triggers are met: demand, funding and readiness
Demand
Funding
Readiness
Signed 2029 or 2030 minimums of 10.5M units or more (today 9.4M / 9.8M), including take-or-pay or prepaid volume
At least $3.5M of committed funding, so cash after the $4.2M payment is $7.5M or more
Supplier confirms installation within 12 months of order at a fixed price; specialty validation plan in place
•  OR: the monthly simulation shows 2+ months below 98% with the molder at its contracted capacity
•  Why 10.5M: signed overflow (~1.6M) would already use two-thirds of the molder ceiling, and fewer than half of the remaining 1.9M unsigned forecast units would exhaust it
•  Arithmetic: $8.2M - $4.2M = $4.0M; plus $3.5M = $7.5M, i.e. the $7.0M floor plus a $0.5M buffer
•  Sources: customer prepayment, or a supplemental loan backed by a signed-volume guarantee; pricing to be negotiated
•  Plan allows +2 months for specialty validation
•  Molder bridge contracted through commissioning
•  Construction inflation re-quoted
Not triggers: 'demand is growing', nonbinding forecasts, peer growth statistics, or a wish to announce capacity publicly.
One customer contract can meet two triggers at once: a signed-volume guarantee raises committed demand and secures the loan.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. 10.5M threshold and $0.5M buffer are our proposals. Internal capacity after specialty scrap ~8.9M + molder 2.5M = ~11.4M of demand coverable without the line.

slides.title: If customer orders fall short, the plan degrades gracefully: in the weak-demand cases the worst outcome is a $0.6M forfeited deposit, never a covenant breach

paragraphs.text: 4  THE PLAN AND GATES
If customer orders fall short, the plan degrades gracefully: in the weak-demand cases the worst outcome is a $0.6M forfeited deposit, never a covenant breach

data: No order (the floor holds); molder to cap, safety stock, ration

paragraphs.text: The case to watch is the last one: demand arrives but funding does not. The board's rule (no breach of the floor) then means accepting 2030 rebid risk. The mitigation is to make customer co-funding (prepayment or a volume guarantee) the price of guaranteed capacity, starting in 2027 negotiations.
Calculation, signed case: $8.8M - $0.6M deposit - $0.16M premiums = ~$8.0M. Slip: $8.8M - $0.6M - $0.36M = ~$7.8M. No-funding: $8.8M - $0.6M - $0.65M = ~$7.6M.
The cash floor holds in every case. Weak demand costs at most $0.6M; the unfunded forecast case is a customer-retention risk, not a cash risk.

Source: Briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis. Cash lows exclude operating cash flow. Funded case assumes $3.5M committed at Gate 2. Premiums at $0.12/unit; lost contribution at $0.45/unit.
